hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to smooth, convex, and often elongated curved structures—such as cylindrical tubes, spherical domes, airships, wheels, or arched wings—predominantly characterized by warm, saturated hues like rust-orange, deep red, golden-yellow, or copper. These features typically present a clean, continuous surface with gradients or highlights indicating curvature and are usually oriented diagonally (often from upper-left to lower-right) or as prominent arcs. The activating objects are consistently set against cool-toned backgrounds of azure blue sky, green foliage, or dark, neutral surfaces, creating a sharp chromatic and luminance contrast. The neuron is invariant to the specific object identity (biological vs. mechanical) and surface texture, provided the large-scale curved form and warm-on-cool contrast are maintained. The feature typically occupies 30–70% of the image area, extending across the center or dominating a specific quadrant like the lower-left.
